question.text: A short peptide on complete hydrolysis produces <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> moles of glycine <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi></mfenced></math>, two moles of leucine <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></mfenced></math> and two moles of valine <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></mfenced></math> per mole of peptide. The number of peptide linkages in it are _____ .

solution.text:
Peptide linkage is also known as peptide bond. It is an amide formed between −COOH and −NH2 group by elimination of a water molecule. It is represented as
-CO-NH-.

Number of peptide linkages =(Total amino acids -1)

Now, given that short peptide on hydrolysis give seven amino acids.
=7-1=6
